in.role: Led Carolina in every receiving category

doFirst.why: Carried forward from this morning, still live until Wednesday. Coker went 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores while McMillan was quiet until garbage time, and 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim costs nothing lasting. Stafford is the drop because a second quarterback behind Josh Allen scores you zero every week — note that is about usable value, not worth: his 303 season projection is real and a QB-thin team in this league would pay for him. If you would rather trade him than bin him, hold the claim.

candidates.note: Do not chase this one. Ownership moved +3.40 on the back of week 1, and the news has already moved the other way: Schefter reports the Raiders believe Bowers misses only one game and returns at the Chargers. The market is pricing a box score; the role has a return date on it.

Free, 83% rostered, and the reason he is a note rather than a card is Isaiah Likely. Likely caught two touchdowns on Sunday night for 27.8 and is the Giants' clear TE1; Pitts caught nothing. Your tight end question for week 2 is Likely over Pitts, not who to add.

A.J. Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks with a high ankle sprain. Doubs, not Mack Hollins, is the beneficiary — Hollins played more snaps but was blocking in a run-heavy plan. He is rostered by a Chem rival whose WR1 just went to injured reserve, which makes this trade leverage more than a wire note.

410 yards and three scores on 56 attempts, and New Orleans are 7.5-point underdogs to Baltimore next. A volume quarterback on a team that trails. Irrelevant now, but this is the shape of the free claim that covers Josh Allen's week 7 bye — and in Chem that claim costs nothing.
